summary: Tested backend Truth-of-State enforcement gate (_derive_verified_block in routers/patrol.py) and frontend evidence-bridging wiring (enforcementEvidenceSync.ts, ApolloContext.tsx). Full backend suite: 218/218 passed (208 prior + 10 new gate tests in test_enforcement_evidence_gate.py), confirming zero regressions from PatrolEventIn/PatrolEventPatch model changes across family.py, family_weekly.py, push.py, admin.py and all prior test files. Frontend unit tests (enforcementEvidenceSync.test.ts, platformCapability.test.ts, securityConfig.test.ts, protectionTruth.test.ts): 27/27 passed. tsc --noEmit: exactly the one expected pre-existing error at app/(tabs)/home.tsx:217, nothing new. Frontend smoke test via Playwright (mobile viewport 375x667): app boots cleanly through onboarding, Home/Guard/Patrol tabs render correctly, MOCK ADAPTER — SIMULATED disclosure shown honestly, real link-check against a known-malicious test URL (http://testsafebrowsing.appspot.com/s/phishing.html, same one used by test_apollo_backend.py) correctly reaches 'barking' state, and tapping 'Block this destination' correctly shows 'Block not verified: Mock adapter (demo): nothing is blocked on this device' / 'Block could not be verified. Apollo is still barking.' — confirming blockEvent() in ApolloContext.tsx still correctly refuses to fabricate a verified block in mock mode. No console errors, no red screen, no spontaneous/unexpected PatrolEvents observed from refresh cycles (evidence array is empty in mock mode as designed).
action_items: OUT OF SCOPE (confirmed, not testable here): Kotlin native files under /app/frontend/modules/apollo-security/android/ (EnforcementEvidence.kt, EnforcementEvidenceTest.kt, DnsPacket.kt edits, ApolloDnsVpnService.kt, ApolloSecurityModule.kt) require a native EAS build + physical Android device to verify. No gradle/kotlinc/JVM available in this sandbox.

Metro cold-start occasionally shows a transient blank screen right after `sudo supervisorctl restart expo`; not observed as a regression this round (app loaded cleanly on first try) but noting the previously-diagnosed pattern per the context note in case it recurs for the next agent.
critical_code_review_comments: _derive_verified_block in routers/patrol.py is well-isolated, pure, and documented; correctly gates on evidence presence, result, enforced_action, mechanism blacklist, and device_id match. Mirrors isVerifiedEnforcement() on the frontend as claimed.
PatrolEventPatch correctly no longer exposes verified_block; verified test that PATCH with verified_block:true in the body is silently ignored by Pydantic and has no effect.
toPatrolEnforcementEvidence() mapping is lossless and does not launder simulated/unverified evidence into a verified shape (verified by dedicated unit test 3).

blockEvent() in ApolloContext.tsx correctly gates evidence attachment on both result.verified AND isVerifiedEnforcement(result.evidence) before ever attaching it -- defense in depth even though backend re-validates independently.
syncEnforcementEvidence()'s evidenceId dedup via AsyncStorage ('apollo.evidence.seen') is capped at 200 entries, reasonable bound.
seed_data_creation: None required beyond what test_enforcement_evidence_gate.py creates/cleans via its own device registrations.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend Truth-of-State gate and frontend evidence-bridging are fully verified and stable. Remaining work for a future round is exclusively the physical-device/native-build verification of the Kotlin module (EnforcementEvidence.kt, ApolloDnsVpnService.kt, ApolloSecurityModule.kt) -- cannot be done in this sandbox (no Android SDK/gradle/JVM). No further backend/frontend regression testing needed for this feature unless the Kotlin bridge introduces new fields that need re-validating against EnforcementEvidenceIn once a physical device test is run.
rca_of_issue: No bugs found this round; all changes (backend gate, frontend sync, ApolloContext wiring) behaved exactly as specified in the review request with no regressions detected.
